ruled_out_vectors.vector: H1: Tick crossing at exact boundary — liquidity not properly added/removed
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Standard Uniswap V3 logic at DynamicHelper.computeSwap:411. Tick crossing check is == comparison. getNextSqrtPriceFromInput rounds conservatively. Battle-tested pattern, no novel attack surface.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H2: Fixed height split rounds to zero on one side — free tokens
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: FixedHelper._splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight:1576 uses mulDivRoundingUp for input (user pays more), calculateFixedSwapByRatioRoundingDown for output (user gets less). Guard at L1656 reverts on zero-value swaps. Rounding consistently favors protocol.
Known design property (L-04). 100% input fee => amountRemainingLessFee = 0 => amountIn = 0 => no swap occurs. Output swaps reject 100% fee at FeeHelper:219. No extraction path.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H4: swapExtraData != 32 bytes — unexpected price movement
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Known issue (L-01). DynamicPoolType:433 defaults to widest price limit. AMM's limitAmount at AMMModule:2156-2173 provides slippage protection separately.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H5: uint256 truncation on cast to uint128 in reserve updates
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMMModule._safeIncrementUint128:3503 and _safeDecrementUint128:3520 use assembly with overflow/underflow checks. Input values come from uint128 storage slots, so truncation can't occur in practice.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H6: Division before multiplication in fee/swap math — precision loss
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All fee calculations use FullMath.mulDiv or mulDivRoundingUp which handle 512-bit intermediate products. TickMath divide-before-multiply is standard V3 lookup table. No precision loss exploitable.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H7-H10: Assembly calldataload, ABI encoding, returndata corruption, memory pointer attacks
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Solidity 0.8.24 strict mode with compiler protections. Assembly uses calldatacopy (not raw calldataload). Memory-safe assembly blocks. No unmasked data flows to arithmetic.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H11: Dust-loop extraction — 100+ tiny swaps to harvest rounding errors
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: FixedHelper dust (L1695-1710) goes to pool state and is distributed to LPs on withdrawal. Rounding consistently favors protocol: output rounds DOWN, input rounds UP. Attacker loses fees each swap. No extraction path.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Probe 2: Forged hook caller — call hooks directly without going through AMM
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: _requireCallerIsAMM() at AMMStandardHook.sol:940-942 guards all hook entry points (lines 110, 159, 253, 312). Returns if msg.sender != AMM address.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Probe 4: Permit mutation — replay with mutated feeOnTop
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeOnTop unsigned is known (rejected submission #8). SWAP_TYPEHASH includes limitAmount which caps total exposure. Signer can't lose more than limitAmount regardless of feeOnTop.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Probe 5: Storage-slot collision — deploy facet that writes to another's slot
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool types are external contracts called via regular calls (not delegatecall). Each stores state keyed by msg.sender (AMM address) in globalState mapping. Diamond storage at 0x9A1D is isolated. No collision path.

theft_theses.thesis: Tick crossing at exact boundary causes liquidity mismatch enabling better-than-market price
Fixed pool height split rounds to zero enabling free tokens on one side
Iterated dust-loop extraction via 100+ tiny swaps in fixed pools
theft_theses.asset: Pool reserves via accumulated rounding errors
